draft.title: Evaluating aesthetic qualities
card: Aesthetic qualities are the features of a text that make it striking, beautiful or moving, such as imagery, sound, rhythm and word choice.
To evaluate them, a reader does more than name a feature. They judge how strongly it affects a reader.
A good evaluation names the feature, explains the effect it creates, and says how well it works with the other features.
Example: in a poem about a storm, short, harsh words and a pounding rhythm may suit the violent scene. Together they make the storm feel fierce.
draft.remember: Evaluating means judging how well features create an effect and work together.

a.q: Which sentence best evaluates the aesthetic qualities of a poem?
opts: The slow rhythm and soft sounds suit the quiet mood well
The poem has four stanzas and uses a slow rhythm
The poet was born in a small country town
The poem is about a quiet evening by the sea
a.why: This sentence names features, links them to the mood and judges that they suit it. The sentence about stanzas only names features and gives no judgement. It is the most tempting wrong option because it mentions rhythm.
a.clue: Look for the option that judges how well features work.

b.q: Leila writes about a film: the music is loud and the colours are bright. Which addition would turn this into an evaluation of aesthetic qualities?
opts: Together they make the carnival scene feel joyful and busy
The film was released in the same year as a famous book
Many people in the audience enjoyed the film's story
The film also has a number of other scenes with music
b.why: Only the first option explains the effect of the features and how they combine to create it. Saying many people enjoyed the story is tempting, but it is about the audience and the plot, not about how the features work together.
b.clue: Which option explains what the features do together?

a.best: The slow rhythm and soft sounds suit the quiet mood well

b.best: Together they make the carnival scene feel joyful and busy

problems.detail: The clue ('what the features do together') echoes the word 'Together' that opens the right option, so a student can match words without understanding evaluation.
Why (b) calls the right answer 'the first option', but options are shown in random order and here it appears second, which would confuse students.

check.summary: The content is accurate and both answers are clear. In question b, the clue echoes the right option's opening word 'Together', and the explanation refers to 'the first option' even though the options are shuffled.
